instrument_or_setup.value: EMPYREAN, PANALYTICAL with Co-Kalpha source; operating voltage 40 kV, operating current 40 mA

key_findings.value: Low intensity XRD peaks of all the elements have vanished after 5 h of milling, indicating the onset of alloying; the diffraction peak intensity of all the elements decreases with milling time.

measurement_conditions.value: scan rate 5 deg min-1; patterns collected after every 5 h of milling (panel a of Fig. 1 includes the 5 h pattern)

purpose.value: To ascertain the alloying behavior during milling and phase evolution of the powder as a function of milling time.

source.reason: XRD was used to study the alloying behavior/phase evolution of the milled powders including the 5 h state; the vanishing of low-intensity elemental peaks is the key 5 h observation.
Milling was carried out with toluene as process control reagent to avoid oxidation.

atmosphere.value: toluene (process control reagent, to avoid oxidation)

source.reason: The sample is defined as the powder state after 5 h of milling; the text states 'Low intensity peaks of all the elements have vanished after 5 h of milling'.
Experimental details describe the milling equipment and conditions used for all milled states including the 5 h state.

processing_steps_notes.value: Planetary ball mill (Model no. PM 400/2, Retsch) at 200 rpm; ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; milling carried out in tungsten carbide (WC) vials with WC balls; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating. 2-3 g of milled powder taken after every 5 h of milling to study phase evolution.

source.reason: The 5 h milled state results from mechanical alloying performed under these conditions up to 5 h of milling.
Elemental Fe is one of the constituent phases whose peaks are indexed in the milled powders; low-intensity peaks have vanished at 5 h but the element remains.
Elemental Mn is one of the constituent phases indexed in the milled powders.
Elemental Ni is one of the constituent phases indexed in the milled powders.
Elemental Al is one of the constituent phases; Al intensity only diminishes after 15 h of milling.
Elemental Si is one of the constituent phases indexed; Si remains even after 35 h of milling.
Elemental C is one of the constituent phases indexed in the pre-milled/milled powders.

At 5 h of milling the powder consists of the elemental phases (low-intensity elemental peaks vanished, indicating onset of alloying); no quantitative microstructure (crystallite size, strain) was reported for the 5 h state (reported only for 25/30/35 h).

overall_structure.value: Mechanically alloyed powder after 5 h of milling showing the onset of alloying: the low-intensity XRD peaks of all constituent elements have vanished. No new intermetallic/solid-solution phase (BCC, gamma-brass type or B2-type) is reported at this stage; the vanishing of low-intensity elemental peaks indicates the initiation of alloying.

source.reason: The 5 h milled powder is characterized only by the phase-evolution XRD study; no new phase has formed at this stage.

unmapped_findings: The 5 h milled state belongs to the milling-time series (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 h) used to track phase evolution; 2-3 g of milled powder was withdrawn after every 5 h of milling for XRD analysis (b0020, figure_001).

During milling the C (interstitial) dissolves faster than the other alloying elements due to its smaller atomic size and higher diffusivity; Al begins to dissolve (intensity diminishes) only after 15 h of milling; after 20 h intense Ni and Mn peaks are no longer evident, and a solid solution is formed after 25 h of milling (b0038, b0058).

The elemental diffraction peaks indexed in the milled powders (relevant to the 5 h state) are Fe (cI2, JCPDS# 00-006-0696), Mn (cI58, JCPDS# 00-032-0637), Ni (cF4, JCPDS# 00-004-0850), Al (cF4, JCPDS# 00-004-0787), Si (cF8, JCPDS# 00-005-0565) and C (hP4, JCPDS# 00-056-0159) (b0038).
